summary: @servicetitan/microfront ships an obfuscated preinstall that downloads the Bun runtime and executes a bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React MicroFrontEnd integration library under the @servicetitan npm scope, but its package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, and setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNN` identifiers and dictionary decoders. On `npm install`, setup.mjs checks for a system `bun` binary and, when absent, downloads a Bun runtime zip from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then runs `execFileSync(<bun>, [math_init.js], {stdio:'inherit'})`. math_init.js is a ~727 KB heavily obfuscated file carrying obfuscator.io fingerprints — a large mixed numeric/string array (`n7gIxM=[...]`), an array-rotation function, a string decoder, and opaque renamed identifiers — and begins with a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header, meaning it is only executable under the fetched Bun runtime and bypasses Node-based inspection. The payload's filename and contents are unrelated to any MicroFrontEnd functionality. The repository URL `github.com/servicetitan/playground.git` does not correspond to a genuine ServiceTitan production package, consistent with scope impersonation targeting ServiceTitan-adjacent developers. Installing the package runs attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
